summary: TRADEOFF is a browser‑based mission design game for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It lets users design a science mission from the bus up: choose instruments, orbit, and launch vehicle, then live with the mass, power, data, and budget consequences. Every decision opens one door and closes another. The game runs entirely in the browser with no backend, using a provisional dataset compiled from public mission literature. It addresses the challenge by making trade‑offs visible and interactive, helping users understand the complexity of mission design. It is important because it lowers the barrier to entry for learning about space mission engineering, making it accessible to students, educators, and enthusiasts without requiring specialized software or expertise.
details: TRADEOFF is a browser-based mission design game that lets users design a science mission from the bus up. Choose instruments, orbit, launch vehicle, then live with mass, power, data, budget consequences. It implements a full mission design loop: briefing → spacecraft → orbit → launch → compatibility review → deterministic simulation → report → hangar. Includes 6 science objectives, 25 components, 15 orbits, 6 launch vehicles, 4 difficulty levels. A 1800-day simulation models eclipse, battery, downlink, degradation, science return. Review screen provides NASA-MDL-style compatibility check with JPL-CML-inspired maturity badge. Report includes score audit, science closure, margins, findings. Hangar stores runs locally with leaderboard and comparison. Sharing via URL-encoded links. Benefits: lowers barrier to entry for learning space mission engineering; makes trade-offs visible and interactive. Impact: educators, students, mission-design teams can iterate designs instantly without specialized software. Tools: React 19, TypeScript, Vite 8, Lucide icons, Fontsource, Puppeteer, Vitest. Creative: arcade-style UI with neon aesthetic, deterministic simulation with real telemetry, procedural mission patches. Factors considered: mass, power, data, pointing, lifetime, cost, radiation, coverage, eclipse, comms geometry.
